subject: Discovery recap + toolchain handoff / next steps for PayFlux POC

Cc: Marc Bell <marc@infraadvisors.io>

Subject: Discovery recap + proposed handoff: SDK/auth/routing + tool patterns

Hi Sana / Liam,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the clear breakdown of PayFlux's three prioritized flows (payment reconciliation QA, merchant support assistant, and fraud-explainability summaries). Quick recap and a proposed handoff plan so we keep momentum: 

1) Deliverables from Redwood (next 10 business days):
- SDK quickstart repo with example server-side routing and client auth patterns (Node + Python).
- Recommended embedding pipeline: per-merchant namespaces, incremental upserts, and a candidate-re-ranker recipe.
- Tool/function calling patterns doc (when to map to a sync tool vs async worker, parallelization, error semantics).

2) Key technical preferences you mentioned:
- Server-side routing for PII-sensitive calls and to centralize rate-limit/billing attribution.
- Short-lived API keys with automated rotation via your KMS.
- Re-ranker to run on top of sparse candidate sets (~50 candidates), prefer light-weight BERT-lite for latency < 120ms.

3) Initial integration choices we recommend:
- Auth: short-lived tokens issued by PayFlux backend -> Redwood Dedicated or Private edge; support for mTLS as option.
- SDK: seed examples will include auth middleware, streaming helper and structured-output validators.
- Routing: policy-driven routing: low-latency region preference -> cost-fallback -> model-variant fallback.
- Tools: define atomic tool interface (name, inputs, allowed side-effects, idempotency flags); allow concurrent tool fan-out for enrichment (e.g., payment-history lookup + external risk service) with a configurable fallback chain.

Attachment: integration-brainstorm.pdf (architectural sketches) and initial-maf.xlsx (MAF / early timeline table).

Ask / next steps:
- Can we schedule a 60-min technical deep dive the week of Oct 5 to walk the SDK quickstart and auth flows?
- Please confirm which environment you want the POC to target (Redwood Hosted sandbox vs. Dedicated eval).

Happy to loop Marissa and Tessa for deeper tech details — copied them here.

Cheers,
Karthik
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Discovery recap + proposed handoff: SDK/auth/routing + tool patterns

Hi all — following up with a more technical sketch of the tool/function calling patterns we recommend for the POC. High level first, then a few concrete examples.

Summary: choose a layered approach that separates (A) read-only enrichment tools, (B) idempotent lookup tools, and (C) mutating tools with explicit transaction boundaries. Use a coordinator (server-side) to fan-out to parallel tools and reconcile results.

Patterns and rationale:
- Tool defi nition schema (used by SDK & control plane): name, version, input_schema, output_schema, side_effects (none | idempotent | destructive), timeout_ms, retry_policy, idempotency_key_required.
- Parallel execution: run read-only enrichment (e.g., payment-history fetch, merchant-config lookup) in parallel; gather results, then pass to re-ranker and decision-tools. This reduces end-to-end latency when tool latencies are independent.
- Error handling: classify errors as transient (retry with backoff), non-retryable (return best-effort with diagnostics), and partial-failure (return partial payload with per-tool error metadata).
- Fallbacks: model-variant fallback, cached-response fallback, and last-known-good (for re-ranker weights).

Concrete examples: 
1) Merchant support assistant (live chat)
- Fan-out: payment-history lookup (100–300ms), refunds-policy (30–80ms) in parallel.
- Re-ranker: lightweight cross-encoder run on top of 30–50 candidates, aim for P95 < 150ms.
- Failure: if re-ranker times out -> use embedding-based lexical scorer as fallback and include trace tag in response.

2) Reconciliation QA (batch)
- Tools: bulk-transaction-join (async worker), anomaly-scanner (async), summarizer (LLM). Use job queue and callback URL; do not block for synchronous tool calls.

Implementation notes for the SDK quickstart:
- Include a ToolClient class with typed tool descriptors and a execute_with_policy(tool, input, policy) helper.
- Provide sample middleware for: token refresh, request attribution headers (x-payflux-merchant-id), and structured-output validation (JSON Schema + Redwood structured output guardrails).

Attachments: I attached a short code sketch inline in the SDK repo and will drop a one-pager in the shared Drive after this thread.

Happy to walk through these in the technical deep dive — Karthik, Tessa: can you propose Wed 10/07 10:00 or Thu 10/08 11:00 ET?

Best,
Marissa

Sana — thanks for the signal and the latency note. We built the Mutual Action Plan draft for the POC and attached it (mutual_action_plan.docx). Highlights:

- Week 1: Sandbox access, SDK quickstart, runbook for short-lived key rotation (we'll provide example Lambda + KMS policy).
- Week 2: Integrate embeddings + initial vector-upsert pipeline; run relevance smoke tests against merchant sample data.
- Week 3: Implement tool fan-out pattern for the support assistant and wire re-ranker; measure P95 latency and adjust batching config.
- Acceptance criteria (POC): successful end-to-end support assistant flow with P95 < 200ms in your staging environment, re-ranker accuracy improvement > 12% over baseline, and documented auth/key rotation tested.

Logistics / asks:
- Please share an initial dataset sample (anonymized) and a contact for on-prem/security to start the KMS/rotation conversation.
- Proposed deep dive: Thu 2026-10-08 11:00 ET (Marissa and I will run a 45-min technical session + 15-min Q&A). If that works we'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep dive.

Tessa Morgan
Engineering Lead, Integrations | Redwood Inference
